semanticsToPreserve.existingEntries: TagHelperFeature.TagHelpers is a getter-only IList<TypeInfo> backed by List<TypeInfo>. The provider never clears it. Preexisting non-discovered entries and preexisting duplicates remain unchanged.
semanticsToPreserve.duplicates: Existing equal entries suppress new additions. Repeated accepted types within or across parts are added only at their first currently absent occurrence. Default assembly discovery already removes repeated assembly identities; explicit AddApplicationPart appends parts without deduplication.
semanticsToPreserve.equality: List<TypeInfo>.Contains uses EqualityComparer<TypeInfo>.Default. Names, FullName strings and reference-identity comparers are not replacements for this equality contract. A prospective hash set would additionally rely on matching hashes.
semanticsToPreserve.order: Existing list prefix and duplicates remain; newly accepted absent types append in part/type enumeration order. IApplicationFeatureProvider<TFeature> explicitly documents the ordered part sequence and precedence use. Replacing the list with a set is not equivalent.
semanticsToPreserve.liveMutation: IncludePart and IncludeType are protected virtual, type-provider Types is an application-extensible IEnumerable<TypeInfo>, and all feature providers receive the same mutable feature. A prior provider may retain the feature. During a later callback/enumerator step it can synchronously add/remove/clear entries; current Contains observes the list after IncludeType returns. Concurrent mutation is not assumed or endorsed.
semanticsToPreserve.snapshotObligation: A once-seeded method-local HashSet would preserve initial duplicates only if used solely as membership metadata, but would miss subsequent externally produced list mutations. Count checks alone miss same-count replacement. No deployed mutation case or failing native test was claimed; this is a source-visible preservation obligation, not a verified product defect.

candidateAssessment.considered: A method-local HashSet<TypeInfo> for accepted-type membership while preserving list order.
reasons: The real framework consumer is opt-in registration, not a render/request hot path.
The actual repository opt-in site supplies one accepted helper; the real built-in source populations are 20 and 3 concrete helper declarations, not evidence of large accepted-type sets.
No real large application or repeated production lifecycle was established that would justify extra membership storage and the preservation burden.
A naive snapshot changes live-list mutation behavior at public extension seams. A safe specialized/fallback design would add complexity without established material benefit.
notClaimed: That a hash set can never help a real larger application.
That runtime performance is unchanged or improved.
That runtime assembly populations, callback reachability or consumer results were exercised by a native test.
